title: Standard Cost Model (SCM) — Draft Working Notes (terminology, open questions, rough schema)
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- We need a Standard Cost Model (SCM) so Console and Optimize can reason about inference economics consistently across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
- This is a working doc to capture debates, unsettled terminology, and a first-pass schema sketch.
- Not billing. Output must be explicitly labeled “technical cost estimate/attribution,” not invoice.

Owners / stakeholders (active in these notes)
- Platform: Priya Natarajan (owner), Jordan Lee (versioning/determinism)
- Telemetry: Logan Wright (lead), Nadia Rahman (token metering)
- Console: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin (integration)
- Optimize: Aditya Rao (PM), Hassan Mirza (eng)
- Runtime: Mateo Alvarez / Sofia Ivanova (signals)
- Unit economics sanity check: Laura Bennett

Working definition (proposed)
SCM = a versioned specification + deterministic calculation rules that produce:
1) Total cost (in USD) for a request or a defined window, AND
2) A breakdown by components (compute, memory, cache, overhead), AND
3) A record of assumptions and a confidence score when signals are missing/approximate.

Key terminology debates
A) “Estimated” vs “Metered attribution”
- Problem: Console wants per-request/per-route costs; Optimize wants what-if comparisons before deployment.
- Draft: treat this as two related modes with the same output shape.
  - Mode 1: ESTIMATE
    - Used for what-if (Optimize), and for Console when telemetry is incomplete or delayed.
    - Inputs: declared/requested params + environment + optional observed signals.
    - Behavior: deterministic calculation with explicit assumptions; may use model/SKU baselines.
  - Mode 2: ATTRIBUTION
    - Used when telemetry signals exist for a specific request_id/span/window.
    - Inputs: observed runtime/telemetry (prefill/decode timing, effective batch size, cache hit rates) + environment metadata.
    - Behavior: compute cost using observed signals; still may require assumptions (e.g., shared overhead allocation).

Open question: do we force a hard split into 2 endpoints (estimate vs attribution) or allow a single endpoint with mode + precedence rules?
- Console prefers a single “explain” that always returns something.
- Telemetry folks prefer strong semantics so we can detect “not actually metered” cases.

B) “Cost” vs “Price”
- SCM outputs COST (technical infra cost) and SHOULD NOT embed customer contract pricing or discounts.
- Still needs USD because Console UX expects dollars. So we need a “cost_to_usd_rate_table” internal mapping per SKU/region/time.
- Output field names should avoid “billing_amount” / “invoice.”

C) Per-token vs per-request vs per-window
- Optimize wants per-token normalized outputs for comparing quantization/batching changes.
- Console wants per-request and aggregated per-route, and possibly token-level views.
- Proposed: base atomic record is “work unit” = request span, which includes token counts, and optionally time slices.

D) “Compute” definition
- Runtime team: true compute is GPU active time; but “active time” is tricky with batching.
- Finance/econ: the relevant cost driver is GPU reservation time (or amortized capacity) regardless of whether kernels were active.
- Proposed: we model compute as “GPU-time allocated” rather than “kernel active time.”
  - For Hosted (shared): attribute GPU-time using effective batch share.
  - For Dedicated: mostly based on reserved capacity time slice; request attribution is secondary and may be normalized.
  - For Private/on-prem: may run without USD (or with customer-provided rates); see Private section below.


Goals to preserve
- Deterministic: same inputs => same outputs. No hidden dependencies on mutable external state without version/time pinning.
- Comparable: two requests across different SKUs can be normalized via published rates + metadata.
- Explainable: every “we assumed X” is returned to client.
- Cardinality-controlled: don’t require high-cardinality tags as mandatory inputs.


SCM v1 boundary proposal (still debated)
In scope for v1:
- GPU compute component
- GPU memory / KV cache footprint component (approximate)
- Cache effects: prefix cache / KV cache hit rate impact on prefill/decode work
- Batching efficiency: effective batch size and/or share fraction
- Small fixed overheads: request routing, serialization (kept as a separate named component with low weight)

Out of scope for v1 (parked):
- Network egress (varies by cloud + customer topology)
- Storage (artifact/model downloads)
- CPU-side inference helpers if not measurable consistently
- Retries induced by client behavior (but we may expose “num_attempts” for explain)


High-level mental model (draft)
TotalCostUSD = Sum(components[i].cost_usd)
Each component is one of:
- compute_gpu
- memory_gpu
- cache_savings (negative cost, optional)
- overhead_platform
- overhead_control_plane (optional)

Where compute_gpu cost is derived from:
- gpu_time_seconds_allocated * gpu_cost_usd_per_second
And gpu_time_seconds_allocated is derived from either:
- attribution: observed prefill/decode time * share factor
- estimate: predicted prefill/decode time from baselines * assumed share factor


Rough schema sketch (NOT FINAL)
Naming conventions
- snake_case
- units embedded either in field name or in a “units” section; prefer in field name for clarity in JSON.
- “*_id” fields are opaque strings.

Request: CostModelRequest (draft)
{
  "scm_version": "v1",
  "mode": "ESTIMATE" | "ATTRIBUTION",

  "context": {
    "tenant_id": "tnt_...",            // required for Console use; Optimize may omit when local
    "deployment_type": "hosted" | "dedicated" | "private",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "cluster_id": "clu_...",           // optional; can be omitted to reduce cardinality
    "sku": "h100-sxm-80gb"             // required for USD mapping unless private w/ customer rates
  },

  "model": {
    "model_id": "llama-3-70b",
    "model_revision": "2025-01-05",    // pin for determinism
    "quant_profile_id": "int8-awq"     // optional; if omitted, assume fp16
  },

  "workload": {
    "request_id": "req_...",           // required for ATTRIBUTION
    "route_id": "/v1/chat/completions",// optional
    "input_tokens": 1234,
    "output_tokens": 256,
    "max_output_tokens": 512,           // optional; helps estimate
    "streaming": true,
    "num_candidates": 1
  },

  "signals": {
    "prefill_time_ms": 85.2,            // ATTRIBUTION preferred
    "decode_time_ms": 210.4,
    "batch_size_effective": 7.3,        // not raw batch size; admission-control adjusted
    "batch_share": 0.12,                // alternative representation, TBD
    "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.61,
    "prefix_cache_hit": false,
    "gpu_mem_bytes_peak": 5.4e10        // optional
  },

  "overrides": {
    "gpu_cost_usd_per_hour": 3.25,      // optional; internal only; used for backfills/testing
    "assume_kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.0     // optional; for estimate mode
  },

  "client": {
    "caller": "console" | "optimize" | "internal",
    "requesting_service": "console-backend",
    "requesting_env": "prod"
  }
}

Response: CostModelResponse (draft)
{
  "scm_version": "v1",
  "mode": "ESTIMATE" | "ATTRIBUTION",
  "determinism": {
    "rate_table_version": "2025-02-01",
    "model_catalog_version": "2025-02-07"
  },

  "total_cost_usd": 0.004231,

  "breakdown": [
    {
      "component": "compute_gpu",
      "cost_usd": 0.00388,
      "quantity": "gpu_time_seconds_allocated",
      "quantity_value": 3.58,
      "unit_cost": "gpu_cost_usd_per_second",
      "unit_cost_value": 0.00108,
      "notes": "gpu_time derived from prefill+decode and batch_share"
    },
    {
      "component": "memory_gpu",
      "cost_usd": 0.00051,
      "quantity": "gpu_mem_gb_seconds",
      "quantity_value": 92.3,
      "unit_cost": "gpu_mem_usd_per_gb_second",
      "unit_cost_value": 0.0000055,
      "notes": "peak mem used when available; otherwise modeled"
    },
    {
      "component": "overhead_platform",
      "cost_usd": 0.00006,
      "quantity": "requests",
      "quantity_value": 1,
      "unit_cost": "overhead_usd_per_request",
      "unit_cost_value": 0.00006,
      "notes": "fixed overhead placeholder"
    }
  ],

  "assumptions": [
    "quant_profile_id missing; assumed fp16 baseline",
    "gpu_mem_bytes_peak missing; estimated from model_id + token counts",
    "kv_cache_hit_rate missing; assumed 0.0 for estimate"
  ],

  "confidence": {
    "score": 0.72,
    "grade": "medium",
    "reasons": [
      "used modeled gpu_mem",
      "used baseline prefill/decode prediction"
    ]
  },

  "validation": {
    "warnings": ["batch_size_effective missing; falling back to batch_share=1.0"],
    "errors": []
  }
}

Notes on schema above
- The above includes nested objects/arrays; the actual API schema can be similar, but the key is stable names + units.
- We need to decide if breakdown is a list of objects vs a map of component->numbers.
  - Console UI likes a stable list ordering + notes.
  - Maps are easy for machines but harder for “notes” and future component expansion.


Open questions (tracked)
1) Required inputs for determinism
- If sku + region are required, then private/on-prem needs an alternate path.
- Proposal:
  - Hosted/Dedicated: region + sku required.
  - Private: allow “cost_rates_profile_id” OR allow returning “cost_units” in non-USD and require customer-supplied mapping.
- Need a firm answer from Private GTM + platform: do we ever show USD in Private? (some private customers will still want USD for internal chargeback).

2) How to represent batching attribution
- Options:
  A) batch_size_effective: float representing average batch size for the request’s decode period.
  B) batch_share: fraction of a GPU-second charged to this request.
- batch_share is “closer to what we need” but hard for runtime to emit reliably.
- batch_size_effective is easier to compute but can be wrong if admission control or micro-batching changes.
- Action: runtime + telemetry to agree on one canonical signal name; see ENG-23141 draft.

3) Cache semantics
- kv_cache_hit_rate: is it “hit rate” across decode steps? across requests? across tokens?
- prefix cache vs kv cache: treat as two components or one “cache_factor”?
- Proposal:
  - prefix_cache_hit: boolean (hit/miss) for prefill cost reduction
  - kv_cache_hit_rate: float 0..1 representing fraction of prefill tokens served from cache (or fraction of layers?); we need a crisp definition.
- Concern: different model families implement caching differently; Applied ML (Maya/Arjun) wants room for “cache_behavior_profile_id”.

4) Quantization profile semantics
- quant_profile_id is required for accurate compute/memory estimation.
- But clients may not have it (or runtime may not tag it consistently at first).
- Proposal:
  - If missing: assume fp16 and lower confidence.
  - If present but unknown: validation error in ATTRIBUTION mode; warning + fallback in ESTIMATE mode.

5) Time versioning for rate tables
- USD rates can change (cloud costs, reserved instances, etc.).
- Console wants stable historical views; Optimize wants “today’s rate.”
- Proposed input field: "rate_table_time": timestamp or date
  - if omitted: default = now (for estimate)
  - for attribution/historical: Console passes request timestamp bucket
- This creates an external dependency that can break determinism unless rate tables are versioned and immutable.

6) Allocation of shared overheads (Hosted)
- Things like control plane overhead, idle GPU time, warm pool.
- Should these be in v1? If excluded, then “cost to us” will be undercounted, but request-to-request comparisons still useful.
- Laura’s note: for Optimize recommendations, relative deltas matter more than absolute, but Console wants totals that “add up” with internal views.
- Proposal: include a small “overhead_platform” component that can be tuned later; keep it explicit so it can be excluded from certain views.

7) Cardinality / dimensions
- Telemetry can’t safely tag everything at per-request level with high-cardinality dimensions.
- We need a minimal “dimension set” required for cost attribution.
- Candidate required dims: deployment_type, region, sku, model_id, quant_profile_id, route_id (maybe), tenant_id (Console only).
- “cluster_id” and “pod_id” should be optional and never required.

8) Validation behavior and error model
- Console UX requirement: if SCM is down or inputs invalid, show partial/fallback instead of blank.
- Engineering requirement: strict validation in attribution mode to avoid silently wrong “metered” claims.
- Proposal:
  - ATTRIBUTION: missing required observed signals => error (or downgrade to ESTIMATE and mark in response mode_changed=true)
  - ESTIMATE: missing signals => assumptions + lower confidence

9) Confidence scoring
- We need a simple confidence that Console can communicate without over-explaining.
- Draft idea: start at 1.0 and multiply penalties per missing/estimated dimension.
  - Missing quant_profile: *0.85
  - Missing cache metrics: *0.9
  - Missing batch metric: *0.8
  - Missing prefill/decode timing (estimate path): *0.75
- Output both numeric score and grade (high/medium/low) with reasons.


Annotated examples (draft)
Example 1: Console request-level attribution (Hosted)
Scenario
- Hosted us-east-1, H100, llama-3-70b, quant=int8-awq
- Request had decent batching (effective ~8) and KV cache hit ~0.6

Input (pseudo)
- mode=ATTRIBUTION
- workload: input_tokens=1500, output_tokens=250
- signals: prefill_time_ms=90, decode_time_ms=220, batch_size_effective=8.1, kv_cache_hit_rate=0.62

Expected response notes
- compute_gpu dominates
- cache hit reduces prefill cost (either as reduced time or as explicit negative component)
- confidence high if quant_profile + timings present
- Console tooltip should say: “This is a technical estimate based on observed runtime signals; not an invoice.”

Example 2: Optimize what-if sweep (Estimate)
Scenario
- Optimize wants to compare 3 candidates:
  A) fp16, batching off, cache cold
  B) int8-awq, batching on, cache cold
  C) int8-awq, batching on, cache warm (kv_cache_hit_rate assumed 0.5)

Input for candidate C (pseudo)
- mode=ESTIMATE
- model: quant_profile_id=int8-awq
- workload: input_tokens=3000, output_tokens=300
- overrides: assume_kv_cache_hit_rate=0.5
- signals: batch_size_effective=12 (provided by Optimize as a target)

Expected behavior
- SCM returns total_cost_usd + breakdown for each candidate
- confidence medium because timings are predicted
- Optimize should refuse to recommend if confidence=low OR if assumptions include “unknown sku cost rates”

Example 3: Dedicated capacity caveat
Scenario
- Dedicated customer pays for reserved GPUs; “cost per request” is an attribution convenience, not actual spend.

Proposal
- In Dedicated mode, return two totals:
  - “marginal_cost_usd” (incremental compute) (might be near zero depending on framing)
  - “allocated_cost_usd” (reservation amortized across usage)

Open question
- Do we expose both in v1? Console likely wants “allocated” for visibility; Optimize might want “marginal” for tuning.
- If we do both, we must be extremely careful about naming and docs.


Notes from discussions (summaries)
- Priya: keep v1 small; ship spec + API first, then enrich signals. But must not paint us into corner on versioning.
- Logan/Nadia: telemetry must carry prefill/decode split and batching metrics; cardinality constraints are real. Avoid requiring route_id if it explodes series.
- Dylan/Chloe: Console needs stable component names and “assumptions” text that can be displayed as tooltips. Also needs safe fallback if API times out.
- Hassan: Optimize needs a batch endpoint eventually, but can start with client-side fanout if limits are clear.
- Arjun: quant profile deltas are not uniform across model families; need “profile metadata” and likely a per-model override mechanism.


Near-term action items (next 1–2 weeks)
- [Jordan] Write ADR draft for versioning + negotiation (header vs path). (Ref: Slack 1738254410)
- [Priya/Logan] Agree minimal required signals for ATTRIBUTION mode.
- [Nadia] Confirm token metering fields (input_tokens/output_tokens) and precedence (metered vs client-reported).
- [Sofia/Mateo] Decide canonical batching metric name and semantics (“batch_size_effective” vs “batch_share”).
- [Arjun] Provide first-pass quant_profile_id list + expected compute/memory multipliers.
- [Dylan] Provide Console breakdown UI sections (what components we actually show in v1).


Risks / pitfalls to avoid
- “Looks like billing”: do not let UI or API naming imply invoice accuracy.
- Silent mode downgrade: if ATTRIBUTION inputs are missing, we must clearly mark we returned an estimate.
- Non-determinism via mutable rate tables or catalog: pin versions in response.
- Overfitting to one SKU or one model family: keep components extensible and versioned.


Appendix: Proposed component list (v1 tentative)
- compute_gpu
- memory_gpu
- cache_effect (optional; could be absorbed into compute)
- overhead_platform
- overhead_control_plane (maybe v2)

Appendix: Field naming bikeshed (parking lot)
- tenant_id vs org_id
- sku vs gpu_sku
- quant_profile_id vs quantization_profile_id
- kv_cache_hit_rate vs kv_cache_reuse_rate

End of notes (draft)
- This doc is intentionally messy. Next step is to crystallize into: (1) Confluence spec v1, (2) ADR on versioning/negotiation, (3) telemetry requirements checklist.
